title: multi-gpu-parallelism-performance-investigation-wip
content:
Status: WIP / notes-for-review
Owner: Jordan Li (eng-serving-runtime)
Goal: Investigate scaling behavior and bottlenecks for multi-GPU model serving in the runtime. Focus areas: tensor parallel vs pipeline parallel scaling, NCCL communication overhead, and interconnect limits (NVLink/PCIe/IB). Produce actionable guidance for default parallelism configs and fallback policies in Dedicated/Private offerings.

Background / Motivation:
- Multiple customers hit scaling regressions when moving from single-GPU to multi-GPU model variants (8+ GPUs). Symptoms: lower-than-expected throughput, spikes in tail latency, and uneven GPU Utilization.
- We need to understand which factors dominate at different model sizes and batch shapes: compute-bound (matmuls), memory/KV-cache overhead, communication (AllReduce/AllGather), or kernel inefficiencies from quantized execution.

High-level hypotheses:
1) Small micro-batch sizes (< 8 tokens/batch per GPU) cause communication overhead (NCCL) to dominate, hurting scaling.
2) Tensor-parallel strategies incur large AllReduce bandwidth, saturating NVLink, so on NVLink-limited topologies scaling flattens quickly.
3) Pipeline parallel improves peak throughput for very large models at cost of increased tail latency due to pipeline bubbles; effectiveness depends on inter-node latency and scheduling.
4) NCCL topology mismatches (mixed PCIe + NVLink across nodes) amplify imbalance — should prefer node-local grouping and endpoint-aware placement.

Test matrix (current experiments):
- Models: 7B, 35B, 70B (FP16 and int8 quantized runs where supported).
- Parallelism modes: data-parallel baseline, tensor-parallel (TP) with varying TP widths, pipeline-parallel (PP) with 2/4 stages, hybrid TP+PP.
- Batch shapes: tiny (1 token x 1 request), small (8 tokens x 4 requests), medium (64 tokens x 16 requests), large (256 tokens x 8 requests).
- Topologies: single node 8x A100(80GB) with NVLink (DGX-style); multi-node 2x 8x A100 over HDR-200 InfiniBand; mixed racks with PCIe-only links between nodes (emulates worst-case cloud placement).
- Metrics: tokens/s throughput (steady-state and warmup), p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi & nvprof), PCIe/NVLink utilization (nvidia-smi dcgm counters), NCCL allreduce/allgather time breakdowns (NCCL tests + runtime traces), kernel-level FLOPS and time breakdown (cublas/cudnn/custom kernels).

Profiling toolchain used:
- Built-in runtime tracing (fine-grained op timings) + nvprof/nsight for kernels.
- NCCL logging enabled (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) and per-rank nvprof counters.
- DCGM for per-GPU link usage.
- Perfetto-style end-to-end traces for request lifecycle (client -> server sched -> GPU exec -> response).

Preliminary results (summary):
- 7B model: scales almost linearly up to 4 GPUs for medium/large batches. For tiny/small batches, scaling flattens at 2 GPUs; CPU/network scheduling overhead dominates and NCCL latency kills throughput.
- 35B model (TP across 4 GPUs): tensor-parallel AllReduce accounted for ~30-45% of total step time on NVLink-only node. On multi-node runs (InfiniBand), AllReduce times increased 1.3x due to extra hop.
- 70B model (hybrid TP+PP across 8 GPUs): pipeline-parallel achieved best peak tokens/s for long sequences, but p99 latency grew 2-3x vs single-node smaller setups. Pipeline bubbles become significant at low interleaving when batch count is low.
- NCCL observations: AllReduce/AllGather phases show clear staircase behavior in logs indicating ring algorithm stepping across GPUs. When NVLink bandwidth per GPU < expected (simulated link throttling), AllReduce time increases superlinearly.
- Interconnect limits: NVLink-local grouping reduces cross-node traffic and improved AllReduce times by ~20% vs naive placement. Mixed PCIe topologies exhibited high variance in per-rank times (SD increased 3x).
- GPU utilization: When communication dominates, we see 10-25% idle time on compute kernels waiting on NCCL, indicating opportunities for overlap or algorithmic changes.

Notable traces / artifacts (attached links in linked_artifacts):
- Trace: 35B-TP-4g-nvlink.trace (high-level op timings + NCCL-phase flags).
- NCCL logs: several runs with ring vs tree algorithm toggles - tree alg reduced latency slightly for small messages, ring better for large payloads.

Immediate takeaways / operational guidance (WIP):
- Default: For hosted API, prefer smaller TP widths + data-parallel for 7B-class models; enable PP only for >32B models where memory pressure forces it.
- Placement: Implement topology-aware scheduling that prefers NVLink-connected GPUs for TP AllReduce groups. Add heuristics to avoid mixing PCIe-only nodes in the same TP group.
- Batch shaping: Encourage batching policies that increase per-GPU tokens for TP; put conservative default micro-batch thresholds (e.g., do not use TP>2 unless effective batch tokens/GPU >= 64).
- NCCL tuning: Experiment with NCCL_ALGO and NCCL_MIN_NRINGS per workload size; fallback to tree algorithm for small RPCs.
- Overlap: Investigate compute-communication overlap (async AllReduce) and kernel fusion opportunities to hide NCCL latency.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Quantify the benefit of tensor-slicing optimizations that reduce AllReduce payload (e.g., reduce precision of gradients/activations in-flight) on inference workloads.
- Can we reliably auto-select TP/PP widths based on observed incoming batch-size distribution? Build a small decision-tree/ML policy.
- Measure impact of NVLink 3 vs NVLink 4 vs H100 NVLink improvements — do hardware upgrades change our heuristics?
- For Dedicated customers across racks, can we provide a placement SLA that guarantees local NVLink groups?

Action items (owner tags):
- Jordan: finalize plots for 35B TP vs PP and add to Confluence (due 2025-02-07).
- Maya: run controlled tests toggling NCCL_ALGO=ring/tree for 7B/35B with small batch shapes, collect per-rank breakdowns (due 2025-02-05).
- Carlos: prototype topology-aware scheduler patch (placement heuristic) and add simulation tests (due 2025-02-14).
- Priya: evaluate pipeline scheduling interleaving parameters and measure p99 tails for customer-like traffic patterns (due 2025-02-10).

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Keep an eye on kernel-level inefficiencies in int8 paths; lower memory usage may improve communication-to-compute ratio but introduce new kernel stalls.
- Consider adding a "comm-estimator" to the runtime planner: given model dims and parallelism config, estimate AllReduce bytes/time and warn if expected communication > threshold.
- Customer-facing copy: we should be explicit in docs about when to choose TP vs PP and the tradeoffs (throughput vs tail-latency).

References / links embedded: see linked_artifacts above + internal PR #412 for preliminary plotting scripts.

-- end WIP --
